meta.chapterLabel: Lesson 14: Giving and Receiving: I Received It from My Friend

items.note: あります (arimasu) is the same word glossed "be, exist" for locations in Lesson 12 — here it expresses possession, literally "a meeting exists [for me]," so the thing had takes が (ga), not を (wo).
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 12: Asking about Places: What Is at Nikko? (matched on target)

items.note: The verb negative. Do not confuse it with じゃありません, the negative of です — that one negates "is/are", this one negates "there is / have".
ありませんでした, not じゃありませんでした — the latter is the past negative of です.

items.scene: used to confirm an offer that seems too generous or unexpected
items.note: Said when someone makes an unexpected offer, to check they really mean it.

items.scene: at the end of a clause, before another statement
items.note: Suffix — attaches after an explanatory clause to give a reason (clause + から (kara)).

items.target: わたしはさむくないですから

items.note: Na-adjective — takes な before a noun, e.g. すてきな スカーフ (a lovely scarf).

items.hint: the particle that marks the giver with もらいます
items.note: Marks the giver with もらいます (moraimasu, 'receive from'); with あげます (agemasu) the same に (ni) marks the receiver instead — see GRAMMAR 1–2.
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 3: Asking the Time: What Time Is It? (matched on english)

items.note: Takes に (ni) for the giver — the opposite direction from あげます (agemasu, give), which takes に for the receiver.
The opposite of かります (karimasu, borrow, this lesson) — かします (kashimasu) is the lender's side of the transaction.
Takes に (ni) for the receiver. Cannot be used when the receiver is the speaker — use くれます (kuremasu), this lesson's exception form, instead.

items.target: スミスさんはなかむらさんにはなをあげました

items.note: Compare with the previous card: あげました (agemashita) and もらいました (moraimashita) describe the same event from the giver's and receiver's side — the に (ni) marks the receiver with あげます but the giver with もらいます.
items.target: なかむらさんはスミスさんにはなをもらいました
スミスさんはあしたかいぎがあります

items.english: Give (to me) (exception form of あげます)
items.note: あげます (agemasu) cannot be used when someone gives something to the speaker — use くれます (kuremasu) instead.
items.reviewNote: Named as an exception to あげます in GRAMMAR 1; not otherwise glossed as a headword in this chapter.

items.english: A friend gave me a scarf.
items.reviewNote: The chapter names くれます as the required exception when the receiver is the speaker but never demonstrates it in a sentence — added a worked example reusing スカーフ and ともだち from this chapter.
items.target: ともだちがわたしにスカーフをくれました

items.note: When counting with あります (arimasu), the number goes directly after が (ga) with no extra particle: noun が [number] あります.
items.target: スミスさんはあしたかいぎが２つあります
items.reading: スミスさんはあしたかいぎがふたつあります

items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 10: Describing Things: It’s Delicious (matched on english) | Excluded as a duplicate of chapter-10/sweater — same word, same gloss, earlier occurrence.

items.note: おみやげ (omiyage) means souvenir/gift; きょうと (Kyouto) is the city Kyoto.
The opposite of かします (kashimasu, lend).

items.hint: a fashion bag like a purse or tote (loanword)
items.note: "Bag" was already かばん (Lesson 2) and ふくろ (Lesson 5, a wrapping/paper bag) — バッグ (baggu) is the katakana loanword for a fashion bag like a purse or tote.
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 2: Possession: Whose Pen Is This? (matched on english)

items.note: A second word for scarf, alongside スカーフ (sukaafu) — both mean the same thing.
The お is an optional honorific prefix (written (お)かね in the source). かね (kane) alone also means money, but おかね (okane) is the everyday form.

items.note: なにも (nanimo, 'nothing/not anything') + a negative verb is the set way to say 'nothing at all' — なにも もらいませんでした (nanimo moraimasendeshita) = 'received nothing.'
items.target: なにももらいませんでした
スミスさん、あしたはいそがしいですか

items.english: Yes, I'm busy. [Because] I have a meeting.
items.note: A second example of から (kara, 'because') attaching after a reason clause — compare with わたしは さむくないですから (watashi wa samukunai desu kara, 'because I'm not cold').
items.reviewNote: Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 16: Making an Invitation: Shall We Go Together? (answer uses clause-final から (かいぎが ありますから) to give a reason, a construction formally taught only in chapter 38)
items.target: はい、いそがしいです。かいぎがありますから

items.note: Combines with きねんび (kinenbi, anniversary) to form けっこんきねんび (kekkonkinenbi, wedding anniversary).
Combines with けっこん (kekkon, wedding) to form けっこんきねんび (kekkonkinenbi, wedding anniversary).
Compound of けっこん (kekkon, wedding/marriage) + きねんび (kinenbi, anniversary).
よく (yoku) also means "often" (Lesson 9, frequency); here it's the manner adverb "well," as in よく にあいますね (yoku niaimasu ne, "it suits you well").
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 9: Doing Things (2): Do You Often Come Here? (matched on target)

items.note: Made of よく (yoku, well) + にあいます (niaimasu, suit/look good on).

items.english: I'm sorry (for what I did a while ago).
items.note: Past-tense form of すみません, used to apologize for something that already happened rather than something happening now.
